anchor.label: Gidney 2025
anchor.citation: Gidney 2025, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits' (arXiv:2505.15917). ~20x physical-qubit reduction vs 2019 from algorithmic + error-correction advances; SAME hardware assumptions.

readiness._meaning: progress toward preconditions; NOT distance to breaking RSA

2Q fidelity method = median_ECR_error; not directly comparable across vendors

logical_qubits.notes: No standing logical qubits. IBM's error-correction work (e.g. qLDPC roadmap) is forward-looking, not always-on capacity on this device.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: WEAKEST-SOURCED FIDELITY IN THE SET — flagged deliberately. IBM does not publish a single fixed per-device 2Q gate fidelity; it publishes live calibration data (drifts daily) and dated medians in papers. Value shown is derived from a dated peer-reviewed median ECR error snapshot (7.57e-3 -> ~0.99243 fidelity) as of 2024-08-01. This is IBM's CZ/ECR two-qubit metric, NOT directly comparable to Google's XEB or trapped-ion RB. Treat as a dated snapshot, not a current value.

single_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Derived from median SX error 2.41e-4 as of 2024-08-01.

error_correction_below_threshold.notes: Not demonstrated below-threshold surface-code scaling on this device in the Willow sense.

systems.notes: IBM does not publish a single fixed two-qubit gate fidelity; it reports live calibration data that drifts daily, alongside dated medians in publications. The value shown is a dated peer-reviewed median, chosen so the figure is reproducible. Heron r2 can execute roughly 5,000 two-qubit gate operations in a circuit — a measure of circuit depth, not gate fidelity.

flags: below-threshold EC demonstrated (load-bearing signal; opens fidelity gate)

logical_qubits.notes: Distance-7 surface code: a single logical qubit from 101 physical qubits, 0.143% error per cycle, beyond breakeven (2.4x its best physical qubit lifetime). This is a demonstration of one below-threshold logical qubit, not a multi-logical-qubit standing register. Recorded as 1 with this explicit caveat rather than 0, because the below-threshold demonstration is the load-bearing signal for the formula.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Google does NOT headline an isolated 2Q RB fidelity. It leads with logical error-per-cycle (0.143% d=7) and random-circuit-sampling XEB. The load-bearing signal for this system is error_correction_below_threshold = true, not a single 2Q gate number. Left null rather than back-converting an XEB figure into a misleadingly comparable 'fidelity'.

t1_coherence_us.notes: Nature paper: mean T1 = 68 us (+/- 13). NOTE press_vs_paper: Google's own blog says 'approaching 100 us'; we cite the peer-reviewed 68 us, not the marketing figure.

error_correction_below_threshold.notes: First clear below-threshold demonstration: logical error suppressed by Lambda = 2.14 +/- 0.02 per +2 code distance, d=3 -> d=5 -> d=7. Strongest such published evidence of any system in this set. Load-bearing for the scoring formula.

cloud_available.notes: Research device; not a general-access cloud machine at publication.

systems.notes: Google's blog describes coherence as approaching 100 microseconds, while the peer-reviewed paper reports a mean T1 of 68 microseconds; the published figure is shown here. Willow's defining result is its demonstrated below-threshold error correction, not any single gate-fidelity number.

logical_qubits.notes: The widely-cited '4 logical qubits, 800x error reduction' is a Microsoft/Quantinuum QEC demonstration using Azure's qubit-virtualization layer, not a standing always-on property of the hardware. Recorded as 0 standing; demo noted here.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Paper value 99.843(5)%. NOTE press_vs_paper: Quantinuum's own press release rounds to '99.9% / three nines'; we cite the peer-reviewed 99.843%.

single_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Quantinuum reports single-qubit fidelity >99.99% in materials; left null pending a paired peer-reviewed/spec-sheet value with a clean method tag rather than a rounded press figure.

t1_coherence_us.notes: Quantinuum's H2 data sheet does not list per-system T1/T2 in microseconds. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ hyperfine qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second-to-minute scale — orders of magnitude longer than the microsecond-scale T1/T2 reported by superconducting systems — but this is a property of the ion physics, not a system-specific calibration figure that meets our sourcing bar. Left null in the microsecond column to preserve cross-system comparability.

t2_coherence_us.notes: Quantinuum's H2 data sheet does not list per-system T1/T2 in microseconds. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ hyperfine qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second-to-minute scale — orders of magnitude longer than the microsecond-scale T1/T2 reported by superconducting systems — but this is a property of the ion physics, not a system-specific calibration figure that meets our sourcing bar. Left null in the microsecond column to preserve cross-system comparability.

error_correction_below_threshold.notes: QEC demonstrations exist (with partners) but below-threshold surface-code scaling in the Willow sense is not the claim here.

systems.notes: With all-to-all connectivity from trapped-ion shuttling, a 56-qubit H2-1 is not meaningfully "100 qubits behind" a 156-qubit superconducting machine — connectivity and gate fidelity trade against raw qubit count. Comparing qubit counts across these architectures is misleading.

physical_qubits.notes: 36 physical Yb-171 ion qubits. DO NOT confuse with #AQ 36 (Algorithmic Qubits) — a coincidentally-equal application benchmark SCORE, not a qubit count. See aq_not_qubit_count.

logical_qubits.notes: IonQ logical qubits are roadmap, not present on Forte.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Vendor page: 2Q gate error ~0.4% -> ~99.6% fidelity, measured by Direct Randomized Benchmarking. Corroborated by peer-reviewed benchmarking of Forte at 30q/#AQ29 (arXiv:2308.05071, DRB across 435 gate pairs).

t1_coherence_us.notes: IonQ's Forte page describes what T1 and T2 mean but does not publish numerical values for the system. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second scale — orders of magnitude longer than superconducting microsecond-scale times — but no Forte-specific number meets our sourcing bar (vendor data sheet or peer-reviewed paper). Vendor does separately publish a SPAM error of ~0.5%.

t2_coherence_us.notes: IonQ's Forte page describes what T1 and T2 mean but does not publish numerical values for the system. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second scale — orders of magnitude longer than superconducting microsecond-scale times — but no Forte-specific number meets our sourcing bar (vendor data sheet or peer-reviewed paper). Vendor does separately publish a SPAM error of ~0.5%.

systems.notes: IonQ's "#AQ 36" is an application-level benchmark score, not a count of qubits; that it happens to equal Forte's 36 physical qubits is a coincidence. The two are unrelated quantities and should not be conflated.

logical_qubits.notes: No standing logical qubits demonstrated on Garnet. IQM's roadmap targets 150-qubit scaling rather than near-term error correction on this device.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Median two-qubit CZ gate fidelity 99.51%, measured across 30 qubit pairs. Maximum on a single pair reaches 99.8%. This is IQM's native two-qubit gate; not directly comparable to Google's XEB, IBM's median ECR, or trapped-ion randomized benchmarking.

t1_coherence_us.notes: The 2408.12433 paper characterizes the 20-qubit Garnet device but does not headline a single median T1 figure in microseconds for the deployed system. A separate 2024 IQM milestone reported T1 ~0.96 ms on a planar transmon test device, but that is a fabrication-quality milestone, not the 20-qubit Garnet's operating spec. Left null rather than mix the two.

error_correction_below_threshold.notes: Below-threshold surface-code scaling has not been demonstrated on Garnet.

cloud_available.notes: Available on AWS Braket (EU Stockholm region), May 2024 onwards.

systems.topology: 20 flux-tunable transmon qubits, square lattice with tunable couplers
systems.notes: Europe's most-deployed superconducting platform, with a peer-reviewed paper publishing every required spec. IQM separately reported a 99.91% two-qubit gate fidelity milestone on a test device in mid-2024 — that figure is for fabrication-quality demonstration, not the operating spec of the 20-qubit Garnet, and is not used here. A larger 54-qubit Emerald QPU is also available on Braket as of 2025; out of scope for this Garnet entry.

flags: analog: no gate-model Shor pathway; N/A is a category difference, not a low score

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Aquila is an ANALOG Hamiltonian simulator (FPQA), not a gate-model machine. It has no discrete two-qubit gate fidelity. Null is the correct, honest value here — NOT a missing number. See analog_not_gate_model.

systems.notes: The largest raw qubit count in the set at 256, but Aquila is an analog Hamiltonian simulator, not a gate-model machine — it has no two-qubit gate fidelity and no gate-model pathway to factoring RSA. It is marked N/A rather than given a low score: a category difference, not a quality judgment.

flags: analog: no gate-model Shor pathway; N/A is a category difference, not a low score

physical_qubits.notes: 100 atoms in analog mode per Pasqal's Orion Beta technical overview (Orion Alpha and Beta share the 100-qubit specification). Pasqal has experimentally trapped over 1,100 atoms in larger arrays separately.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Orion Alpha operates in analog mode (Hamiltonian evolution via Rydberg interactions), not as a gate-model machine. It has no discrete two-qubit gate fidelity in the standard sense. Pasqal's roadmap targets gate-based digital operation in future generations (Orion Gamma onwards).

t1_coherence_us.notes: Pasqal reports coherence on the tens-of-milliseconds scale for neutral-atom Rydberg qubits, but does not publish a per-system T1/T2 spec in microseconds.

cloud_available.notes: Available via Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Marketplace, and Pasqal's own user portal.

systems.topology: reconfigurable neutral-atom array (Rydberg), analog Hamiltonian evolution
systems.notes: Pasqal's first-generation production neutral-atom QPU, deployed in HPC centers (Genci in France, Forschungszentrum Juelich in Germany). Like QuEra Aquila, it operates as an analog Hamiltonian simulator rather than a gate-model machine — marked N/A as a category difference, not a quality judgment. Pasqal's roadmap (Orion Gamma 2026, Vela, Pegasus, Centaurus through 2030) targets gate-based digital operation with eventual logical qubits.

physical_qubits.notes: 1,180 atoms loaded in a 1,225-site array. First system to cross 1,000 physical qubits. Sourcing note: the announcement was carried widely in press; the underlying qubit-count and readout claims trace to Atom Computing and to the peer-reviewed PRX Quantum readout paper (Yb-171 nuclear spin). Press-only restatements do not themselves clear the bar.

logical_qubits.notes: Microsoft/Atom '24 entangled / 28 corrected logical qubits' (Nov 2024) is a QEC demonstration via Azure's virtualization layer, not standing hardware capacity. Recorded as 0 standing; demo noted.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: 99.6% reported via Microsoft (integration partner, vendor_published). This is a LATER (Nov 2024) milestone, not the spec of the Oct 2023 announcement system — _as_of reflects that. Method tag is generic ('vendor_reported') because the partner blog does not state the benchmarking protocol; flagged low-confidence-on-method accordingly.

t1_coherence_us.notes: Neutral-atom 171Yb nuclear-spin qubits have demonstrated coherence on the tens-of-seconds scale in vendor materials (the widely-cited 40-second figure) — far longer than superconducting microsecond-scale T1/T2 — but this is reported as a qubit-memory record, not as the system-level T1/T2 specification used here. Left null in the microsecond column rather than force a non-comparable figure into it.

t2_coherence_us.notes: Neutral-atom 171Yb nuclear-spin qubits have demonstrated coherence on the tens-of-seconds scale in vendor materials (the widely-cited 40-second figure) — far longer than superconducting microsecond-scale T1/T2 — but this is reported as a qubit-memory record, not as the system-level T1/T2 specification used here. Left null in the microsecond column rather than force a non-comparable figure into it.

cloud_available.notes: The 1,180-qubit next-gen system was in development at announcement; not a general cloud machine then. Marked false with caveat rather than asserting access we cannot source.

systems.notes: The highest physical qubit count of any scored system. The qubit count comes from a 2023 announcement and the gate fidelity from a 2024 partner publication — different dates and sources, shown with their respective dates rather than blended into a single figure.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: Rigetti reports TWO 2Q fidelities: 99.0% median iSWAP (universal gate) and 99.5% median fSim (specialized, for RCS). Headline value here is the 99.0% iSWAP because iSWAP is the general-purpose universal gate relevant to a Shor-type circuit; the 99.5% fSim is noted but not used as the headline to avoid overstating general-purpose fidelity.

t1_coherence_us.notes: Rigetti cites improved T1 baseline (SQMS/Fermilab metal-deposition work) qualitatively; no paired peer-reviewed/spec numeric us value sourced to the bar. Null rather than estimate.

cloud_available.notes: Available on Rigetti QCS at launch; Braket + Azure stated as coming Q1 2025.

systems.notes: Specifications are vendor-published (an investor press release); no peer-reviewed paper was available for these figures. Rigetti reports two distinct two-qubit fidelities — 99.0% for the general-purpose iSWAP gate and 99.5% for the specialized fSim gate. The general-purpose figure is used here.

logical_qubits.notes: A later device, Zuchongzhi 3.2 (107q, Dec 2025), is reported to demonstrate below-threshold QEC — out of scope for this 3.0 entry but a future trajectory/scored candidate.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity.notes: 99.62% two-qubit (simultaneous) gate fidelity per published PRL.

t1_coherence_us.notes: 72 us reported as average coherence time. Reported as a single coherence figure in the paper; placed in T1 with this caveat rather than split into separate T1/T2.

t2_coherence_us.notes: Paper reports an average coherence (72 us) rather than separately-stated T1 and T2. Not duplicated into T2.

error_correction_below_threshold.notes: 3.0 itself is an advantage/RCS demonstration, not below-threshold QEC. (3.2 successor reportedly is — future entry.)

cloud_available.notes: 3.0-series reported as opened for commercial use via China Telecom's Tianyan cloud platform (Oct 2025). Access may be region-constrained; flag if a conservative stance is preferred. Set true on the basis of the cloud availability report; revisit in Chat D if region-gating warrants a separate field.

systems.notes: The best-sourced entry in the set: a peer-reviewed Physical Review Letters paper reporting every required figure. Its readout fidelity differs between the preprint (99.18%) and the published version (99.13%); the published journal value is shown.

presentation.region_note: Cloud access reported via China Telecom's Tianyan platform and may be region-constrained. Accessibility is not a threat input — it does not affect the score; shown here as a presentation-layer flag only.

announced_not_scored.reason: Roadmap / fusion-based architecture targeting ~1M physical qubits; no peer-reviewed or vendor-published specs for our required fields (per-device 2Q gate fidelity, T1/T2 in our sense) on a deployed machine. Does not clear the §4 bar.
announced_not_scored.notes: Footnote only. Revisit if qualifying specs are published.

announced_not_scored.reason: Photonic (CV / GBS) architecture. Published work (e.g. Borealis GBS in Nature) is real but does not map onto the gate-model 2Q-fidelity / T1-T2 schema this index scores. No qualifying values for our required fields.
announced_not_scored.notes: Footnote only. Photonic CV systems are a structural mismatch for the launch schema, similar in spirit to the analog caveat.

announced_not_scored.reason: Boson 4, available on Google Cloud Marketplace, is a single cat-qubit chip (not a multi-qubit processor) — it demonstrates a >7-minute bit-flip suppression record but does not have the physical_qubits + two_qubit_gate_fidelity combination this schema scores. Multi-qubit follow-ons (Helium 16-qubit, Lithium) are on the roadmap, not deployed.
announced_not_scored.notes: Important architectural alternative — cat qubits target hardware-level bit-flip protection so error correction only needs to handle phase flips. Worth revisiting when Helium or later deploys with published multi-qubit specs.

announced_not_scored.reason: Diraq has a peer-reviewed Nature paper demonstrating >99% two-qubit CZ gate fidelity on industrially-fabricated silicon quantum-dot devices (collaboration with imec, 300mm CMOS) — peer-reviewed credentials, but the demonstrations are on two-qubit double-quantum-dot devices, not a deployed N-qubit processor.
announced_not_scored.notes: Silicon spin qubits offer a manufacturing-scalability story unique among the candidates. Worth revisiting when a multi-qubit Diraq processor with published system-level specs ships.
